subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nano Ecotoxicology
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Nano Ecotoxicology.

hook.text: Nano TiO₂ washed from sunscreen into the ocean inhibits algae growth — the base of the marine food chain.

buildup.text: Nanoparticles aggregate differently in saltwater versus freshwater — toxicity varies with the environmental medium.

discovery.text: Daphnia, zebrafish, and algae are standard test organisms — their nano sensitivity reveals ecosystem-level risks.

twist.text: Lab conditions rarely match real ecosystems — natural organic matter coats particles, changing their behavior entirely.

climax.text: Mesocosm studies simulate real ecosystems — tracking nano fate across water, sediment, and organisms simultaneously.

punchline.text: What is safe in a lab beaker may harm an entire ecosystem — context matters.

quiz.question: Why do lab ecotoxicity results for nanoparticles not always predict real-world effects?
options: Lab organisms are immune to nanoparticle effects
Natural organic matter and varying water chemistry change nanoparticle behavior in real ecosystems
Lab tests use much higher concentrations than exist in nature
